newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait agrees new troop U.S. deployment.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait agrees new troop U.S. deployment.

text.p: Kuwait on Monday approved a U.S. request to deploy several thousand more ground troops in the Gulf Arab state amid fresh tension with former occupier Iraq, a Kuwaiti official said.
"Yes, we have agreed," the official, who declined to be identified, said by telephone. He said the deployment would be a little less than the 5,000 troops proposed by Washington.
He said the decision was taken at a meeting of senior Kuwaiti government officials. The Clinton administration on
Friday announced it had ordered 5,000 army troops from Fort Hood, Texas, to join forces already in the Gulf in preparation for possible military action against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, on a visit to the Gulf to rally the Gulf War alliance against Saddam, on Sunday asked Kuwait's emir, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, for permission to proceed with the plan.
Diplomats said they had expected the Kuwaitis to agree despite the apparent reluctance of Kuwait's Gulf Arab neighbours to participate in a U.S. military buildup in the region.
They said the reason was that the ground troops would be seen as a defensive force, in sharp contrast to the deployment last week of strike aircraft.

"It's one thing to send in ground troops -- a few thousand men are not going to be able to invade Iraq. It can easily be presented as a defensive measure," one envoy said. "But it's quite another to send in strike aircraft that can fly all the way to Baghdad."

U.S. officials have said the Fort Hood troops -- members of two battalions and a Brigade Combat Team headquarters as well as backup maintenance and medical staff -- would be deployed under Exercise Intrinsic Action, a programme begun last year to train Kuwaiti soldiers.

The United States has already sent eight F-117A stealth fighters with laser-guided bombs to Kuwait and four Vietnam-era B-52 heavy bombers armed with cruise missiles to the Indian Ocean Island of Diego Garcia.
Within days, the force is scheduled to include two aircraft carriers with a total of more than 150 Navy aircraft and over 20 other warships and submarines, many armed with cruise missiles.
